title: Physical acceptance — Workshop OS v11.28 UI13 Appliance Settings
body:
## Purpose

Run and record physical WS350 acceptance for the **exact v11.28 UI13 artifact locked below**.

This issue is the canonical physical-acceptance record for UI13. It does **not** claim acceptance has already happened.

## Frozen acceptance source

- PR: #109 — `Finish Workshop OS v11.28 UI13 Appliance Settings`
- Source branch: `feature/ui12-settings-control-center`
- Frozen acceptance branch: `acceptance/v11.28-ui13-appliance-settings`
- Exact source head: `3672a6f0947af0c890a4f7a79c28b140c901425b`
- Build identity: `Workshop OS v11.28 UI13 Appliance Settings`
- UI schema: `UI13`
- Board: `ws_lcd_350`
- Source state entering this gate: **implemented + built + tested by exact-head CI only**

The acceptance branch points directly at the exact source head above. Any later source change is a different candidate and requires new artifact identity and a new acceptance reset.

The final source tree is byte-identical to the previously audited `5b3da1a8882912e5193df8f7fad2ddb209b7257c` candidate: the intervening release-metadata experiment was fully reverted, and GitHub compare reports no changed files between those tree states. Acceptance nevertheless follows the final exact commit SHA above and its own exact-head CI evidence.

`releases/current.json` identifies UI13 / PR #109 as the active source acceptance candidate, while `releases/device-update.json` deliberately continues to publish the separate v11.26 UI11 OTA candidate until a later binary-publication step. Accepted source and stable remain unchanged.

## Exact artifact identity — LOCKED FOR PHYSICAL TEST

Exact-head UI13 Actions run: `34366597025`

- UI13 gate result: **PASS**
- OTA filename: `BambuHelper-ws_lcd_350-Workshop-OS-v11.28-UI13-Appliance-Settings-CI-OTA.bin`
- OTA size: `2334176` bytes
- OTA SHA-256: `8b7ab683879803b37669b675442bc40df4918a7c83947ddff187c9fb4935c0d0`
- Actions artifact ID: `10110277120`
- Artifact ZIP digest: `sha256:a1e02914b963849a66fcedb374205cbba5a3c95e3177ab8782187251fbc1aef2`
- Artifact expiry: `2026-12-08T14:53:25Z`

The downloaded Actions artifact was independently inspected after CI. Its `BUILD-REPORT.txt` records:

- `source_head_sha=3672a6f0947af0c890a4f7a79c28b140c901425b`
- `result=BUILD_PASS`
- `release_state=IMPLEMENTED_BUILT_TESTED_BY_CI_ONLY`
- `product_finish=APPLIED`
- `published_candidate=NO`
- `physical_acceptance=REQUIRED`
- `stable_promotion=FORBIDDEN`
- `ota_size=2334176`
- `ota_sha256=8b7ab683879803b37669b675442bc40df4918a7c83947ddff187c9fb4935c0d0`

Independent local verification confirms the same OTA byte count and SHA-256 and the same ZIP digest GitHub recorded. ESP image structural verification also confirms a valid ESP-IDF ESP32-S3 application image with six contained segments, matching ESP checksum `0xEB`, matching appended ESP image SHA-256 `f0a171a316972e3ab4a1ab70120ef235d784341502eee4c100371d7680bf398e`, and no unexplained trailing bytes.

The final source-state housekeeping did **not** alter firmware bytes: the OTA SHA-256 remains identical to the previously audited polished UI13 build. Acceptance still follows the final exact source head and exact-head artifact above.

**If source SHA, OTA size, OTA SHA-256, or artifact identity differs, stop. That is not this acceptance candidate.**

## Exact-head automated gates

All required workflows on exact head `3672a6f0947af0c890a4f7a79c28b140c901425b` passed:

- Validate — run `34366597032` — **PASS**
- Validate accepted static installer — run `34366597047` — **PASS**
- Workshop OS Firmware Gate — run `34366597044` — **PASS**
- Workshop OS UI13 Appliance Settings Gate — run `34366597025` — **PASS**
- Release Gate — run `34366597023` — **PASS**

This evidence advances the source only to **built/tested by CI**. It is not runtime, production, physical, accepted, or stable evidence.

## Automated non-hardware audit

The exact artifact has also been checked without hardware for the boundaries CI cannot express as a single release-state flag:

- UI13 build identity is embedded exactly once.
- Intended product surfaces are embedded, including Display & Appearance, Sounds & Alerts, Printer & Power, Software Update, and Local Portal functionality.
- Update copy explicitly says on-device install is not enabled in this build.
- Recovery rejects `Full.bin` as normal application firmware and keeps Full/`0x0` recovery separate from OTA.
- Portal-session security and same-origin rejection paths are present.
- `TEST / NO CODE`, `OPENAI_API_KEY`, OpenAI-style `sk-...`, GitHub PAT, AWS AKIA, JWT-like, and `setInsecure` markers were not found.
- Inventory-inference implementation markers `matchSpoolByColor`, `matchSpoolByMaterial`, `resolveSpool`, and `resolveProfile` were not found.
- Exact binary contains `AMS telemetry - inventory identity remains explicit`.
- Routine Settings strings do not expose hidden hold semantics; the remaining `Hold to Stop` and `Hold to Apply` prompts are the intended guarded cases.
- PR #109 had no unresolved inline review threads during the automated audit.

These are **static/artifact checks only** and do not satisfy any real-device checklist item below.

## Physical acceptance checklist

### 1. Install, boot, identity
- [ ] Flash/install the exact locked OTA on a WS350 already using the compatible Workshop OS partition layout.
- [ ] Device boots normally without recovery loop or boot loop.
- [ ] About/System reports v11.28 / UI13 as expected.
- [ ] Reboot returns to a healthy usable state.
- [ ] Record device/hardware identifier and installed version.

### 2. Product-level 480×320 finish
- [ ] Home, Printer, Tools, and Settings are readable at normal workshop viewing distance.
- [ ] Primary navigation is clearly `Home · Printer · Tools · Settings`.
- [ ] Routine controls are reliably finger-sized, including screen edges/corners.
- [ ] Back and primary actions are obvious and consistently placed.
- [ ] No routine task requires a hidden long-press/tap-hold gesture.
- [ ] Selected, disabled, loading, stale, error, unavailable, and unknown states are distinguishable.
- [ ] No text clips, overlaps, wraps awkwardly, or renders outside intended bounds.
- [ ] Spacing, hierarchy, typography, cards, controls, and state treatment feel consistent across all primary screens.
- [ ] Offline/degraded states use warning semantics rather than destructive/fault styling.
- [ ] Red is reserved for actual fault/destructive meaning.
- [ ] Motion/feedback is calm and does not create distracting flicker or unnecessary animation.

### 3. Settings architecture
- [ ] Settings root shows **Display & Appearance**, **Sounds & Alerts**, **Network**, **Printer & Power**, and **System**.
- [ ] Each destination opens the expected screen and returns reliably.
- [ ] Boolean settings use clear switch behavior.
- [ ] Numeric/preset settings use visible decrement/increment controls.
- [ ] Read-only information does not look tappable when it is not.
- [ ] User-facing copy reads as product language, not engineering/acceptance jargon.

### 4. Display & Appearance
- [ ] Brightness changes visibly and persists as intended.
- [ ] Standby brightness works.
- [ ] Night Mode works according to configured behavior.
- [ ] After Print options are understandable and functional.
- [ ] Finish timeout adjustment works.
- [ ] Animated Progress setting behaves as represented.
- [ ] Standby/ambient and wake behavior remain reliable.

### 5. Sounds & Alerts
- [ ] Event Sounds toggle works.
- [ ] Touch Sounds toggle works.
- [ ] Bed Cooled Alert works where applicable.
- [ ] Printer Alerts screen works.
- [ ] Severity and presentation controls behave as shown.
- [ ] Alert Sound / Status Light / Wake Display controls behave as shown where supported.
- [ ] Speaker test/output works.
- [ ] Microphone/MIC ECHO path works where supported.

### 6. Network and Local Portal
- [ ] Network screen accurately reports connected/offline state.
- [ ] Current local address is accurate when connected.
- [ ] Local Hostname/mDNS setting behaves as represented.
- [ ] Show IP at Startup behaves as represented.
- [ ] Ordinary touchscreen Network does not expose static IP/gateway/subnet/DNS engineering editors.
- [ ] Local Portal handoff is deliberate and clear.
- [ ] Primary System/Network surfaces do not expose the rotating portal code.
- [ ] Deliberate Local Portal view displays the reboot-scoped code only when explicitly opened.
- [ ] Portal remains authenticated; presentation of the code does not bypass session/same-origin protections.
- [ ] Wi-Fi reconnects after reboot and after a realistic network interruption.

### 7. Printer & Power
- [ ] Printer connection state matches the real printer.
- [ ] Smart-plug mapping/readiness state is accurate.
- [ ] First enable of Automatic Power Off shows the explicit safety confirmation.
- [ ] Cancel leaves auto-off disabled.
- [ ] Enable activates the intended policy only after confirmation.
- [ ] Auto-Off Delay adjustment works.
- [ ] Cancel on Door works as represented.
- [ ] Advanced plug addressing/type/wiring remains outside normal touchscreen Settings.
- [ ] Power-off during an active print receives the intended stronger protection/warning.

### 8. Printer control safety
- [ ] Chamber light ON/OFF works.
- [ ] Pause → Resume works under a safe test condition.
- [ ] Stop requires the intended guarded hold with visible progress/feedback.
- [ ] Smart-plug printer power works when mapped.
- [ ] No printer command is sent when printer connectivity/state makes it unavailable.
- [ ] Disconnection/stale state fails closed rather than showing invented live state.

### 9. Inventory truth boundary
- [ ] AMS/material telemetry does not silently assign Filament Inventory spool identity.
- [ ] Unknown spool/inventory identity remains visibly Unknown when authoritative identity is unavailable.
- [ ] No quantity, owner, location, printer assignment, feeder/AMS placement, or spool identity is invented by Workshop OS.
- [ ] Printer telemetry and authoritative inventory data remain visually/semantically distinguishable where both appear.

### 10. System, diagnostics, persistence
- [ ] Device Health reflects local hardware/runtime health rather than merely network connectivity.
- [ ] Connectivity is shown separately from Device Health.
- [ ] Date & Time controls work and persist.
- [ ] Software Update truthfully states that on-device install is not enabled in this build.
- [ ] Software Update does not present Full-image/`0x0` migration as normal OTA.
- [ ] Diagnostics reports touch/recovery/connectivity accurately.
- [ ] Settings persist across reboot.
- [ ] Printer configuration persists across reboot.
- [ ] Portal access code rotates on reboot as designed.
- [ ] Time/locale behavior remains correct after reboot.

### 11. Recovery and failure states
- [ ] Existing compatible-layout OTA path remains functional.
- [ ] Recovery remains available and distinct from normal OTA.
- [ ] No Waveshare Home ↔ Workshop OS cross-line migration is attempted through OTA; full-image migration remains the approved `0x0` service/recovery path.
- [ ] Known-good rollback/recovery path remains available.
- [ ] Disconnect Wi-Fi and verify unavailable/stale state without invented current state.
- [ ] Disconnect printer connectivity and verify fail-closed control behavior.
- [ ] Reconnect and verify normal recovery without unnecessary factory reset.
- [ ] Failed settings/actions preserve prior valid configuration where applicable.

### 12. Physical evidence capture
- [ ] Capture representative sanitized framebuffer/screenshots for Home, Printer, Settings root, each Settings destination, System, and key error/degraded states.
- [ ] Confirm `system-portal` evidence redacts the rotating portal credential before retained output is written.
- [ ] Do not retain credential-bearing printer configuration/settings exports.
- [ ] Add photos/video where physical touch behavior, destructive guards, screen readability, or defects are better demonstrated visually.

## Evidence required at completion

Record:

- Device/hardware identifier
- Date/time of physical test
- Exact source SHA
- Exact OTA filename, byte size, and SHA-256
- Installed version shown by device
- PASS / FAIL / N/A for every applicable checklist item
- Reason for every N/A
- Photos/video and sanitized framebuffer evidence where useful
- Every defect/blocker discovered
- Recovery/rollback result if exercised
- Final physical acceptance result: **PASS** or **FAIL**

## Release rule

Do **not** merge #109 because CI is green alone. Do **not** publish/promote UI13 as stable and do not replace the current stable channel until this exact artifact has a recorded physical PASS with no unresolved acceptance-blocking defect.

If physical acceptance passes, the follow-up release/promotion work must preserve the **exact accepted bytes** and provenance. It must not rebuild a different binary and call it accepted.
